mainTopic: The cleaning substances for testing stains (רוק תפל, מי גריסין, urine, rubbing and order), and a new משנה on a וסת based on body signs
overview: The amud begins by finishing an earlier point: a liquid on a garment counts only if the owner is bothered by it (הקפיד). The גמרא then explains the cleaning substances that the משנה lists for testing a stain. רוק תפל is saliva of someone who has eaten nothing from the evening onward. רבי יוחנן adds that midnight must pass while he sleeps, and dozing (מתנמנם) also counts. Speaking most of three hours' worth of speech in the morning cancels it. For מי גריסין, the גמרא rejects a proof for ריש לקיש and notes that רבי יהודה requires boiling bean liquid used before salt is added. It proves from three פסוקים that עובר means 'before.' Urine must ferment for three days, and רבי יוחנן says these measures still need more detail. Whether a back-and-forth rub counts as one rubbing or two stays a תיקו, and אביי reconciles two ברייתות about using the substances out of order. A new משנה then teaches that body signs like yawning or sneezing can set a woman's וסת, and the גמרא explains that this is a וסת of the body rather than of days. It then asks how 'שופעת' can be a warning sign, and עולא בריה דרב עילאי begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rule applies only if he was bothered by it
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of an earlier discussion: the liquid on the garment counts only if the person was particular (הקפיד) about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was bothered by the liquid being there, then yes, it counts. If he was not bothered, then it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an earlier discussion about a liquid on a garment. The rule depends on whether the person cared about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not automatic. It depends on the person's attitude. If he is הקפיד (does not want the liquid there), it counts as significant and has an effect on the garment. If he does not mind, it has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: He was particular or bothered by it; he did not want it there
Yes
If not

steps.whatToRemember: A person's הקפדה (being bothered) can decide whether something counts legally.

phrases.english: If he was particular about it —
phrases.notes: This finishes an earlier discussion about a liquid on a garment. He means the person did not want the liquid there.

phrases.english: yes; if not — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The liquid has an effect only when the owner is particular about it.

steps.title: The ברייתא defines רוק תפל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רוק תפל is, and a ברייתא answers: saliva of someone who has not tasted anything 'מבערב.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רוק תפל? A ברייתא taught: any saliva of a person who has not tasted anything since the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains a term from the משנה, רוק תפל, by quoting a ברייתא. This sets up the next steps, which will argue over what 'מבערב' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saliva of someone who has not eaten is stronger, which is why it is used to test stains. The ברייתא defines it by time: no food 'מבערב.' The exact meaning of that word is the question the next steps will discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: Saliva of someone who has not eaten; literally 'tasteless saliva'
Since the evening, from the evening onward
Tasted, ate

phrases.english: What is tasteless saliva?
It was taught: any where he did not taste
anything since the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רוק תפל is saliva of someone who has not tasted anything מבערב.

steps.title: רב פפא's first reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא thinks the ברייתא means someone who did not eat anything at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, sitting before רבא, wanted to say: this matches the one who said he did not eat anything at night.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא suggests a way to read the ברייתא's word 'מבערב.' This sets up רבא's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא reads the ברייתא as 'did not eat in the evening/night.' On that reading, eating at the evening meal would already ruin the saliva.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say; he wanted to suggest
In front of him, before him
At night, in the evening

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa, before Rava, thought to say,
it is like one who said
he did not taste anything at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an interpretation of the ברייתא from step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed reading: רוק תפל means he ate nothing at night.

steps.title: רבא corrects him from the exact wording
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the ברייתא says 'מבערב' (since the evening), not 'בערב' (in the evening). The word is meant to exclude someone who got up early and ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Does it say 'in the evening'? It says 'since the evening.' This excludes a case where he got up early and ate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב פפא's reading by focusing on one small letter, the מ in מבערב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בערב' would mean he ate nothing at the evening. 'מבערב' means from the evening onward, so even if he ate in the evening, it is fine as long as he ate nothing afterward. What ruins it is getting up early in the morning and eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually teach? (questioning the exact wording)
To exclude
Who got up early and ate

steps.confusionAlert: Do not miss the tiny difference between בערב and מבערב. The whole argument depends on that one letter מ.
steps.whatToRemember: רוק תפל: no eating from the evening onward. Eating early in the morning ruins it.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Does it teach 'in the evening'?
It teaches 'since the evening,'
phrases.notes: So he could have eaten in the evening itself, as long as he ate nothing after that.

phrases.english: to exclude where he rose early and ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's reading
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב פפא's interpretation of the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He read the word as בערב, but the ברייתא says מבערב, which means 'from the evening onward.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן adds midnight and sleep
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן defines רוק תפל as saliva where midnight passed while the person was asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רוק תפל? Any saliva where midnight passed over him while he was asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: A second definition of רוק תפל is given, and it adds two conditions: midnight and sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke only about not eating. רבי יוחנן adds that midnight must pass and that the person must be sleeping at the time. That second condition, sleep, is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Midnight
Sleep
Passed over him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is tasteless saliva?
Any where midnight passed over him
and while asleep.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵיזֶהוּ רוֹק תָּפֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an additional definition of the same term
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רוק תפל requires that midnight passed while the person was asleep.

steps.title: Challenge: a source says sleep does not matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether sleep really decides it, since a source says that sleeping all day does not make רוק תפל, while staying awake all night does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the matter depends on sleep? But we learned: if he slept the whole day, it is not רוק תפל; if he was awake the whole night, it is רוק תפל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's sleep condition from an earlier source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source says a person who stayed awake all night still has רוק תפל. That suggests sleep is not needed, which contradicts רבי יוחנן's rule that midnight must pass while asleep.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say?
The matter depends on
Was awake

phrases.english: Is that to say the matter depends on sleep?
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: יָשַׁן כׇּל הַיּוֹם — אֵין זֶה רוֹק תָּפֵל,
phrases.english: if he slept the whole day — this is not tasteless saliva,

phrases.aramaic: נֵיעוֹר כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה — הֲרֵי זֶה רוֹק תָּפֵל!
phrases.english: if he was awake the whole night — this is tasteless saliva!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's definition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source calls the saliva of someone awake all night רוק תפל, so sleep seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Answer: the source means he was dozing
steps.stepSummary: The 'awake all night' case in the source is about someone who was dozing, not fully awake.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about someone who was dozing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case in the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Awake all night' does not mean fully alert. He was half-asleep, which counts enough like sleep for רבי יוחנן's rule, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that case
Dozing, half-asleep

steps.whatToRemember: Dozing counts for רוק תפל, so even the 'awake all night' case fits רבי יוחנן's rule.

phrases.english: There, it is with one who is dozing.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case in the source that said 'awake the whole night.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Awake all night' means fully awake, so sleep would not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was dozing, which counts like sleep, so רבי יוחנן's rule stands.

steps.title: What exactly is dozing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of מתנמנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of dozing?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 7 depends on the word 'dozing,' so the גמרא asks what it means. This sets up רב אשי's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since dozing now decides the law, the גמרא needs a clear line between dozing, sleeping, and being awake.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of dozing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the term used in step 7

steps.title: רב אשי describes dozing
steps.stepSummary: Dozing means half-asleep and half-awake: he answers when called but cannot reason, and he remembers when reminded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Asleep but not asleep, awake but not awake. When people call him he answers, but he cannot give a reasoned answer, and when they remind him of something he remembers it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a practical description of what it looks like to be dozing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is about how his mind is working. He responds and can remember things when reminded, so he is not deeply asleep. But he cannot think through an argument, so he is not truly awake.

keyTerms.meaning: Asleep and not asleep
Awake and not awake
To give back a reasoned answer
They remind him

steps.whatToRemember: מתנמנם: he can answer and remember when reminded, but he cannot reason. That half-sleep counts for רוק תפל.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
asleep and not asleep,
awake and not awake,
when they call him — he answers,
but he does not know how to give back a reasoned answer,
and when they remind him — he remembers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: נִים וְלָא נִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dozing is a half-sleep state: he responds and remembers when reminded, but cannot reason.

steps.title: Morning learning cancels רוק תפל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if someone got up early and learned his chapter aloud, his saliva is no longer רוק תפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if a person got up early and recited his chapter of learning, that is not רוק תפל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a new limit to רוק תפל: speaking out loud in the morning takes away its special status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, רוק תפל depended on sleep and midnight. This ברייתא adds that talking also matters. Even after a night of sleep, if he already learned aloud, his saliva no longer counts as רוק תפל.

keyTerms.meaning: He got up early in the morning
He recited his chapter of learning out loud
'Tasteless' saliva, the strong morning saliva used to clean a stain

phrases.english: It was taught: if he got up early and recited his chapter
this is not tasteless saliva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another condition to the definition of רוק תפל after the discussion of sleep and dozing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning aloud after getting up cancels the status of רוק תפל.

steps.title: How much talking cancels it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much speaking is needed to cancel רוק תפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a measure: how much does he have to say before his saliva stops being רוק תפל? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'recited his chapter' but gave no amount. The גמרא wants to know whether a few words are enough or whether a larger amount is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much? A request for a measure

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: He means how much talking is needed before the saliva loses its strength.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure behind the rule stated in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of speech that cancels רוק תפל.

steps.title: Most of three hours' worth of speech
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that once he has said most of what he usually says in three hours, it is no longer רוק תפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר שילא said in the name of רב אשי in the name of רבי אלעזר: any time he has spoken most of his normal speech for three hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The measure is most of the amount a person normally says in three hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure is personal: it depends on how much this person usually talks. A few words do not cancel רוק תפל. Only most of three hours' worth of his normal speech does.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of his normal amount of speech
Three hours

steps.whatToRemember: רוק תפל is canceled once a person has spoken most of what he normally says in three hours.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Sheila said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said, Rabbi Elazar said:
any case where most of his speech has come out
of three hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא, אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Most of the speech he normally says in three hours.

steps.title: Does chewed beans support ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's מי גריסין, made by chewing beans, and suggests it supports ריש לקיש, who says רוק תפל must be added to every cleaning substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Bean liquid' means chewing split beans, etc. Shall we say this supports ריש לקיש, who said that רוק תפל has to be with each and every one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item in the משנה, מי גריסין, and tries to use it as a proof for ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that רוק תפל must be mixed with each of the cleaning substances. The משנה says the beans are chewed, which mixes them with saliva. The גמרא suggests the משנה requires chewing for exactly that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquid from split beans, one of the cleaning substances
Chewing
Shall we say this supports him?
Each and every one

phrases.english: Liquid from split beans
means chewing split beans, etc.
Shall we say this supports Reish Lakish,
as Reish Lakish said:
tasteless saliva must be
with each and every one?
phrases.notes: Each one of the other cleaning substances listed in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רוק תפל to the next item in the משנה, מי גריסין.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's rule that רוק תפל must be added to each cleaning substance.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's requirement that the beans be chewed, which mixes them with saliva.

steps.title: Maybe it is the mouth's heat
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: maybe the chewing helps because of the warmth of the mouth, not because of the saliva.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the warmth of the mouth is what helps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Chewing may be needed for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chewing does two things: it adds saliva and it warms the beans. If the warmth is what makes the bean liquid work, the משנה tells us nothing about saliva, so ריש לקיש is not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, used to reject a proof
The warmth of the mouth
Helps, is effective

phrases.english: Perhaps the heat of the mouth is what helps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not ריש לקיש's opinion itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Chewing could be required for the mouth's warmth rather than for the saliva.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה does not follow רבי יהודה, who says bean liquid must be boiling and must be used before salt is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, bean liquid must be boiling, and before salt is put into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different opinion exists about how מי גריסין must be prepared, and that the משנה does not follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the bean liquid as made by chewing. רבי יהודה requires bean liquid that is boiling and has not yet had salt added. These are different ways of preparing it, so the משנה is not following רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow the opinion of...
Boiling
Here it means 'before'
Salt

steps.confusionAlert: Here עובר does not mean 'passes' or 'transgresses.' It means 'before,' and the next steps prove it.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
bean liquid must be boiling,
and before one puts salt into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with מי גריסין and notes an opinion the משנה does not follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, bean liquid works only when boiling and before salt is added, and the משנה does not follow him.

steps.title: How do we know עובר means 'before'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the word עובר can mean 'before.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word עובר means 'ahead of, before'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on a word in רבי יהודה's ברייתא and asks for proof of its meaning. This sets up the פסוקים that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually עובר means 'passing.' The גמרא wants a source showing that it can also mean 'coming first,' which is how רבי יהודה used it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where can we tell? What shows this?
A word meaning 'coming first, before'

phrases.english: From where may it be inferred that this word 'over'
is a term meaning 'before'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי עוֹבֵר לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַקְדּוֹמֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that עובר means 'before.'

steps.title: Proof from אחימעץ outrunning the כושי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings the פסוק where אחימעץ ran and 'ויעבור' the כושי, meaning he got ahead of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the פסוק says, 'And אחימעץ ran by way of the plain, and overtook the כושי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer: in this פסוק, ויעבור means that אחימעץ got ahead of the כושי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two runners were carrying news. When אחימעץ 'עבר' the כושי, it means he passed him and came first. This shows that the root עבר can mean 'ahead of.'

keyTerms.meaning: As the פסוק says
And he passed ahead of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: as the verse states:
"And Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain
and overran the Cushite."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In שמואל ב 18:23, ויעבור means that אחימעץ got ahead of the כושי.

steps.title: אביי's proof: יעקב went before them
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings the פסוק about יעקב: 'והוא עבר לפניהם,' meaning he went ahead of his family.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: from here, 'And he went before them.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different פסוק as proof that עבר can mean 'going ahead.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יעקב went to meet עשו, he went in front of his family. The word עבר there clearly describes going first.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, from this פסוק
He went ahead of them

phrases.english: Abaye said: from here:
"And he passed before them,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second source for the same point as step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In בראשית 33:3, עבר לפניהם means going ahead of them.

steps.title: Third proof: their king passed before them
steps.stepSummary: Another option is the פסוק in מיכה: 'ויעבור מלכם לפניהם וה׳ בראשם,' where the king goes first, at their head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is from here: 'And their king passed before them, and ה׳ at their head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third possible source for the meaning of עובר, which closes this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק, ויעבור is paired with 'בראשם,' at their head. That makes it especially clear that the word means leading in front.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead
At their head, leading them

steps.whatToRemember: עובר in רבי יהודה's ברייתא means 'before,' and the גמרא proves this meaning from three פסוקים.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is from here:
"And their king passed before them
and the Lord at their head."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, alternative source for the meaning of עובר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In מיכה 2:13, ויעבור together with בראשם shows that it means going first.

steps.title: How long urine must ferment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'urine that fermented,' and a ברייתא defines fermenting as three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'urine that fermented.' A ברייתא taught: how long must it ferment? Three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה, 'urine that fermented,' and brings a ברייתא that says how long the fermenting takes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the urine must be fermented, without giving a time. The ברייתא fills in that missing detail: three days.

keyTerms.meaning: Urine, one of the seven cleaning substances
Became fermented or sour
Fermenting, souring

phrases.english: Urine that fermented.
It was taught: how long is their fermenting?
Three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵי רַגְלַיִם שֶׁהֶחְמִיצוּ. תָּנָא: כַּמָּה חִימּוּצָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of the word עובר to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urine counts as fermented once it has stood for three days.

steps.title: The measures for stains need further measures
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the חכמים' measures for כתמים are still unclear, and lists unanswered questions about which urine to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: all the measures the חכמים gave for stains themselves need a measure. Should the urine come from a child or an old person, from a man or a woman? Should it be kept covered or uncovered? Should it be from the summer or the rainy season?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says that even after the rules are given, many details are still missing, and he shows this using the urine as an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even 'urine fermented three days' is not exact enough, because urine differs depending on whose it is and how and when it was kept. Each of these differences could change how strongly it cleans, and the rule does not tell us which one to use.

keyTerms.meaning: The measures or amounts set by the חכמים
Blood stains found on a garment
Their measures themselves need further definition
Covered or uncovered

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
All the measures of the Sages regarding stains
need a measure for their measure.
phrases.notes: The rules aren't exact enough yet; they need more detail before you can actually use them.

phrases.english: Of a young person or of an old person,
of a man or of a woman,
covered or uncovered,
in the summer days or in the rainy days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל שִׁיעוּרֵי חֲכָמִים בִּכְתָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the three-day rule by showing that the urine is still not fully defined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measures for כתמים are not fully defined; for example, the type of urine to use is unclear.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that these rules are hard to apply exactly in practice, even after the ברייתא's detail.

steps.title: Is a back-and-forth rub one rubbing or two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule of rubbing three times. רבי ירמיה asks whether moving the hand forward and back counts as one rubbing or two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one must rub three times. רבי ירמיה asked: does moving forward and back count as one rubbing, or does forward and back count as two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, and רבי ירמיה asks how the three rubbings should be counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires three rubbings but does not say what one rubbing is. If forward and back is one, you need three full back-and-forth motions. If it is two, fewer motions are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: To rub, scrub
He asked, raised a question he could not settle
Bringing forward and bringing back, a back-and-forth motion

phrases.english: And one must rub three times.
Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
Is bringing forward and bringing back one,
or perhaps bringing forward and bringing back is two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה, about rubbing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one forward-and-back motion counts as one rubbing or two.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the answer is and concludes תיקו: the question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer? Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot answer רבי ירמיה's question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source was found to decide the question. The counting of the rubbings stays uncertain.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: How to count the three rubbings is a תיקו. We do not know whether forward and back is one rubbing or two.

phrases.english: What is it? Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי ירמיה's question without an answer.

steps.title: Using the second group before the first: one ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about applying the substances out of order. A ברייתא says that if the second group was used first, the second group counts and the first does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he applied them not in their order. The Rabbis taught: if he put the second ones before the first ones, one ברייתא teaches that the second ones count for him and the first ones do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of using the substances out of order and brings the first of two ברייתות about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says that doing them out of order accomplishes nothing. This ברייתא is more specific: the second group still counts, and only the first group has to be done again.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in their proper order
Put before, did earlier
They count for him
The first group / the second group of substances

steps.confusionAlert: 'First' and 'second' are groups from the משנה's list, not single items. The first group is saliva, bean liquid and urine. The second group is the remaining four substances.

phrases.english: If he applied them not in their order.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה, which says this accomplishes nothing.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he put the second ones before the first ones,
one teaches:
the second ones count for him,
the first ones do not count for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה, about the order of the substances.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the second group came first, the second group counts and the first group does not.

steps.title: A second ברייתא rules the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says the opposite: the first group counts and the second group does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another ברייתא teaches: the first ones count for him, and the second ones do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that contradicts the first. This sets up a contradiction that the גמרא will need to resolve next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות deal with the same case, where the second group was used before the first. Yet they reach opposite results about which group counts, so the גמרא now has a clash between two teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one

phrases.english: And another one teaches:
the first ones count for him,
the second ones do not count for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ruling for the same case as the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's ruling that the second group counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות rule in opposite ways on the same case, so they appear to contradict each other.

steps.title: אביי shows the two teachings actually agree
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that both ברייתות agree: the second group used counts. The word 'first' in the second ברייתא means first in the משנה's order, which was actually used second.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: both teachings agree that the substances used second count, and the ones used first do not. So what does the other teaching mean by 'first'? It means first in the order of the משנה, which here were used second.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction from the last step by showing that the two ברייתות are saying the same thing in different words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'first' can mean two things: first in the משנה's list, or first in the order the person used them. אביי says the second ברייתא's 'first' means first in the list. Those were the substances this person used second, so both ברייתות agree that what was used second counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one: both sources agree
According to their order, meaning the order listed in the משנה
In their application: the order he actually used them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two ברייתות disagree about which group counts. They both say the group used last counts. They only use the word 'first' differently.
steps.whatToRemember: When the substances are used out of order, the ones used last count. 'First' in one ברייתא means first in the משנה's list, not first in use.

phrases.english: Abaye said: both this one and that one
the second ones count for him, and not the first ones
And what does 'first ones' mean?
First according to their order [in the משנה],
but second in the order he applied them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִידִי וְאִידִי שְׁנִיִּים עָלוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the contradiction raised in step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word: 'first' means first in the list, not first in use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to disagree about whether the first or second group counts
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree that the group used last counts

steps.title: New משנה: a וסת based on body signs
steps.stepSummary: A woman whose period comes after a regular body sign, such as yawning, sneezing or stomach pain, has a וסת. She is impure only from when she sees blood. Three times sets the pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any woman who has a וסת: her own time is enough. These are the signs that make a וסת: she yawns, sneezes, feels pain near her stomach or in her lower belly, has a discharge, or gets shivers, and anything similar. If a sign repeats three times, it becomes a וסת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists body signs that can become a woman's regular pattern before her period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman with a set pattern is not made impure backward in time. She is impure only from the moment she sees. The משנה adds that a body sign, not just a date, can be that pattern, once it happens three times.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's regular, predictable pattern for when her period comes
Her time is enough: she is impure only from the moment she sees, not backward
She yawns
She sneezes
Shivers or shudders
She set it: the pattern became fixed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a וסת can be tied to the body, not only to the calendar.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי' כׇּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת
phrases.english: MISHNA: Any woman who has a fixed cycle,
her time is enough.
phrases.notes: He means she becomes impure only from when she sees blood, with no worry about the time before.

phrases.english: And these are the cycles:
she yawns, or she sneezes,
or she feels pain near her stomach, or in her lower abdomen,
or she has a discharge,
or a kind of shivering takes hold of her,
and likewise anything similar to these.
And any sign that she set for herself three times,
that is a fixed cycle.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A body sign repeated three times before her period becomes a וסת, and she is impure only from when she sees.

steps.title: Didn't we already learn this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the rule 'any woman with a וסת, her time is enough' was already taught in an earlier משנה, so why repeat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this once: any woman who has a וסת, her time is enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for repeating a rule that was already taught earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a משנה does not say the same thing twice for no reason. Since the exact same words appeared earlier, this משנה seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned this once: a challenge that something is repeated

phrases.english: GEMARA: We already learned this once:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ!
phrases.english: Any woman who has a fixed cycle, her time is enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opening line of the new משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The opening line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rule was already taught earlier, so repeating it seems pointless

steps.title: Days versus body
steps.stepSummary: The earlier משנה was about a וסת of days. This משנה is about a וסת of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it means a וסת of days. Here, it means a וסת of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two משניות are talking about two different kinds of וסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה spoke about a pattern set by the calendar, like a certain number of days. This משנה adds a new kind of pattern set by body signs. So it is not a repeat: it teaches that the same rule also applies to a body-based וסת.

keyTerms.meaning: Cycles based on days, a calendar pattern
Cycles based on the body, a pattern set by physical signs

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of וסת: one set by days and one set by body signs. The rule 'her time is enough' applies to both.

phrases.english: There, it is about cycles of days;
here, it is about cycles of the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בִּוְסָתוֹת דְּיוֹמֵי הָכָא בִּוְסָתוֹת דְּגוּפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each משנה deals with a different kind of וסת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to teach the same rule
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier one is about a וסת of days, and this one is about a וסת of the body

steps.title: The משנה's list proves it is about the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the משנה's own list of signs, all of which are physical, to show that this משנה is about a וסת of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the משנה teaches: these are the cycles: she was yawning, sneezing, feeling pain near her stomach or in her lower belly, or having a discharge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by quoting the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item in the משנה's list is a body sign, not a date. That shows the משנה is talking about a וסת of the body, just as the answer said.

keyTerms.meaning: The opening of her stomach, the upper belly area
The lower part of her abdomen
She has a discharge

phrases.english: As it teaches: these are the cycles:
she was yawning, sneezing,
or feeling pain near her stomach, or in her lower abdomen,
or having a discharge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 29 from the משנה's own words
steps.raayaObject: That this משנה deals with a וסת of the body
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's list of physical signs

steps.title: How can a flowing discharge be a warning sign?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's listing of 'שופעת' as a body sign. A flowing discharge seems to be the period itself, not a sign before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She discharges'? But she is flowing anyway!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks one sign from the משנה's list, 'שופעת', and asks how it can be a warning sign at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A וסת הגוף means a body feeling that comes before the bleeding and announces it. The גמרא reads 'שופעת' as a steady flow of blood. If so, it is the period itself, and it cannot be the sign that comes before the period.

keyTerms.meaning: She discharges or flows; one of the body signs listed in the משנה
She keeps on flowing; the bleeding of the period itself
A period pattern set by a regular body sign, such as yawning or sneezing

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a discharge is impure. The question is whether it can count as a sign that comes before the period, as opposed to being the period itself.

phrases.english: She discharges?
But she is continuously flowing!
phrases.notes: The גמרא means that a flow of blood is the period itself, not a sign that the period is coming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 30 proved from the משנה's list of signs that the משנה is about a וסת הגוף. Now the גמרא questions one item on that list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's inclusion of 'שופעת' among the body signs of a וסת הגוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A body sign has to come before the bleeding. A flowing discharge seems to be the bleeding itself, so it cannot be a sign that comes before it.

steps.title: עולא בריה דרב עילאי begins to answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces עולא בריה דרב עילאי, who will explain what 'שופעת' means in the משנה. His explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא, the son of רב עילאי, said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It brings in the sage who will answer the question about 'שופעת', and his actual answer comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 31 assumed that 'שופעת' means a flow of blood. We should expect עולא's answer to explain the word in a way that makes it a real sign that comes before the period.

phrases.english: Ulla, son of Rav Ilai, said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the question asked in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Will explain what the word means (the full answer continues in the next lines).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שופעת' means a flow of period blood, which is the period itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated here. עולא's explanation follows in the next lines.
